item.title: Innovation, Security, and Resilience: Firm Strategy and Industrial Dynamics amid Critical Infrastructure Disruption
item.content:encoded:
Michele Acciaro, Copenhagen Business School

Martin Jes Iversen, Copenhagen Business School

Ioannis Lagoudis, University of Piraeus

Iryna Savelieva, Odesa National Maritime University

Dong Yang, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University

Kum Fai Yuen, Nanyang Technological University

Critical infrastructure (CI) systems, such as energy, transportation, telecommunications, and water, form the backbone of modern economies. These systems face unprecedented challenges from technological disruptions, geopolitical tensions, environmental pressures, and evolving security threats, from cyber-attacks and supply chain vulnerabilities to climate impacts. Virtually no firm can consider itself independent from CI, as infrastructure disruptions cascade through supply chains, energy failures halt production, and transportation bottlenecks constrain competitiveness.

The deep interconnection between innovation and security, conceptualized as the 'security-innovation nexus', has emerged as a defining feature of contemporary political economy. Understanding CI security innovation requires engaging with complex interdependencies where technological capabilities, industrial structures, geopolitical strategies, and security co-evolve. Innovation systems frameworks offer powerful analytical lenses for this purpose, yet CI systems remain relatively understudied within innovation studies despite their strategic importance.

Appel publié par Industry and Innovation. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Innovation Systems, Governance, and Geopolitics - Technological Innovation Systems (TIS) approach for CI security and how security-focused innovation systems emerge and evolve
  • Innovation Systems, Governance, and Geopolitics - Sectoral and technological innovation systems in CI security, knowledge bases, and actor networks
  • Innovation Systems, Governance, and Geopolitics - Regulatory innovation and multi-level governance approaches balancing security, safety, and economic efficiency
  • Innovation Systems, Governance, and Geopolitics - Geopolitical competition, technology sovereignty, and industrial policy effects on CI innovation systems
  • Firm Strategies, Organizational Innovation, and Resilience - Organizational innovation and adaptation in response to CI system vulnerabilities
  • Firm Strategies, Organizational Innovation, and Resilience - Firm strategies, organizational innovation, and business models for infrastructure security
  • Firm Strategies, Organizational Innovation, and Resilience - Resilience, supply chain security, and infrastructure interdependencies
  • Digital Transformation, Sustainability Transitions, and Human Factors - Digital transformation, automation, and cybersecurity in critical infrastructure
  • Digital Transformation, Sustainability Transitions, and Human Factors - Sustainability transitions and the security-environment nexus
  • Digital Transformation, Sustainability Transitions, and Human Factors - Socio-technical transitions, ethics, and human factors in CI sectors
  • Multi-Level Transitions and Sectoral Applications - Multi-level dynamics of transitions with focus on critical infrastructure
  • Multi-Level Transitions and Sectoral Applications - Sectoral applications including energy, transportation, telecommunications, water, financial systems, healthcare, and space infrastructure
